requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change edits `TypeCollector` so that a broken key contract no longer crashes analysis. In both the property loop and the field loop it does two things. After a member's key kind clashes with the other members (MsgPack005 is reported), it skips that member with `continue`. It also adds a member to the int-key or string-key map only if that key is not already there, instead of calling `Dictionary.Add` blindly. It adds analyzer tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types (MsgPack004, 015, 003, 005, and a test that MsgPack011/016/017 are not reported). It also adds run-time execution tests and a README section.
story.why: Issue 2234: since 3.1.1 the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for types marked `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. The change implies the cause was an exception in `TypeCollector` on invalid key contracts (duplicate or mixed keys), which killed analysis. Nothing in the diff touches any code that checks `SuppressSourceGeneration`. So whether the general symptom is fixed (e.g. MsgPack004 on a suppressed type with no key problem) rests on the new tests passing, not on visible code.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section describing run-time and analyzer behaviour.
An execution test project file checks the run-time dynamic-resolver round trip and that no formatter is generated. This is run-time behaviour, not the analyzer.
The duplicate-key and mixed-key guards also apply to normal (non-suppressed) types. There is a dedicated test for generated types.
story.confidence_overview: High that the new guards stop the `Dictionary.Add` duplicate-key exception and the null `intKey!.Value` dereference on the property path, which the tests exercise. Low on the field path: no test uses fields with duplicate or mixed keys. Medium-to-low that the root cause of issue 2234 is addressed, because no suppression-gating logic changed. The MsgPack004/015/003 tests are the only evidence and must pass in the real run.

findings.description: Claim C13 disputed: Over-citation in README.md lines 1620-1633: C13 only describes the section heading and the lists of analyzer rules that apply vs do not apply (lines 1625-1632), omitting lines 1622-1623 which document [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], state that no formatter is generated, and claim that dynamic resolvers use reflection and are not AOT-safe (whereas MessagePack dynamic resolvers use runtime IL code generation where supported, as noted just above at line 1617).

No code that checks `SuppressSourceGeneration` is changed. The fix only stops crashes on duplicate or mixed keys. If the 3.1.1 regression was that suppressed types skip analysis entirely, then the MsgPack004/015/003 tests would fail and the issue would be unfixed. These tests are the only evidence for the main symptom, so check that they really pass and that they fail on 3.1.1.

Duplicate-key members are now silently dropped instead of throwing. This also applies to non-suppressed types. If the generator does not stop on the MsgPack005 error, it could emit a formatter that silently omits a member. The diff does not show where generation halts on errors.
The field-path guards (1148, 1163-1166, 1179-1182) are not exercised by any test. All the new duplicate and mixed-key tests use properties.
The README says MsgPack012 (accessibility) is still reported for suppressed types. No test checks this.

README.md line 1630 documents that MsgPack012 (resolver accessibility) is still validated for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types, but SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs contains no test verifying that MsgPack012 is reported when SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

On lines 1035 and 1175, hiddenIntKey++ is incremented while constructing MemberSerializationInfo before lines 1039 and 1179 check !stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey) and discard duplicate string-key members. Any subsequent string-keyed member on a non-suppressed type receives a non-contiguous IntKey greater than or equal to stringMembers.Count when the source generator runs on code with duplicate string keys.
